title: MIPI D-PHY lane pair (clock lane + data lane): HS bursts (SoT, B8 sync, bytes, EoT), escape mode (LPDT, ULPS, trigger), and the same lane decoded on the receive side

regs.name: CMD
regs.desc: Lane requests (latched by the core and served from the next LP-11 stop, HS first)

fields.desc: write 1: request an HS burst; its bytes come from HS_TX
write 1: request escape mode with ESC.esc_cmd (a second request before it is served replaces the command)
write 1: clear the receiver's sticky error
0x87 LPDT (bytes from LPDT), 0x78 ULPS, 0x46 trigger reset; taken by CMD.esc_req

regs.name: HS_TX
regs.desc: HS payload byte; one byte every eight clocks, and the burst ends (EoT) when the next byte is not there in time

regs.name: LPDT
regs.desc: LPDT byte; the escape ends after a byte with last set, or when the next byte is not there in time

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Byte decoded from the receive lane (HS payload or LPDT); reading RX frees it

regs.name: RX_ESC
regs.desc: Escape command decoded from the receive lane; reading RX_ESC frees it

fields.desc: an HS burst is being decoded
the receive lane is in ULPS

irqs.name: HS_SENT
irqs.desc: an HS burst finished and the lane is back in LP-11

irqs.name: ERROR
irqs.desc: the receiver saw a protocol violation (bad HS sync, invalid HS level, unknown escape command, illegal LP sequence); sticky in the core, so the bit is set again on every clock until CMD.irq_clear

notes: d_lp_p / d_lp_n / d_hs_p / d_hs_n / d_hs_en (data lane), c_lp_p / c_lp_n / c_hs_p / c_hs_n / c_hs_en (clock lane) and r_lp_p / r_lp_n / r_hs_p / r_hs_n / r_hs_en (the receive lane) pass through unchanged. Each LP state and each HS or LPDT bit lasts one PCLK.

A byte takes eight clocks on the lane: HS_TX and LPDT must be written, and RX read, at that rate (one holding register each; a byte arriving with RX full is dropped, RX_OVF). The escape command encoding is simplified to one bit per clock (LP-10 one, LP-00 zero).
